name: Triple Match 3D
full_sequence:
9 portrait shots (1290x2796, no device frame). They work as three acts: a brand hero, a captioned challenge trio, then five uncaptioned gameplay spectacle shots.

ACT 1: BRAND HERO
1. Logo plus story scene, no caption. A chunky two-tone stacked wordmark on a dark rounded plate sits at 12-28% of the height. Below it an overloaded little car drives up a winding road toward the viewer, piled with the game's matchable objects (luggage, beach ball, camera, guitar, donut, cheese). Loose items and coins fly off it. Pastel world landmarks, a rainbow hot-air balloon and a big foreground bush frame the scene on a high-key sky-blue gradient. Job: brand recall and "a heap of cute stuff" told as a story, not as UI. It does not explain the mechanic.

ACT 2: CHALLENGE TRIO (captioned, background colored to the theme, game background removed)
2. Cats on a purple field. The caption is a counting question, with the small number in pink. Under it float the game's own goal cards (cat faces with counts), acting as an answer key. The pile below is zoomed in and bleeds off both edges: about 40 big objects (cats, yarn, milk bottles, toy mice, litter trays), with the cat faces turned to camera. The bottom tray is empty and all four boosters show padlocks (a new player). Job: teach the core loop in one glance and invite the viewer to start counting.
3. Rubber ducks on a teal field. The same question structure with a bigger number in yellow. One goal card. It is a bath-toy pile (sponges, soap, beach balls, toy boats, buckets). The tray holds exactly 3 ducks, frozen one beat before they clear. Two boosters are now unlocked and show counts. Job: show the match moment and escalate.
4. Dogs on a navy field. The caption opens with "And" plus the biggest number, in blue, so it continues the previous shot's question. Four goal cards. The pile is dogs, bowls, food bags, slippers and squeaky chickens. All boosters are unlocked. Job: pay off the chain. Unlocking across shots 2 to 4 quietly implies progression.

ACT 3: SPECTACLE QUINTET (raw gameplay, flat charcoal background, full HUD with level number, countdown timer and crown counter, no captions)
5. Red fast-food pile. Three burgers enlarged about 2-3x with a gold rim glow and sparkle trail, flying to the tray. Job: the match payoff.
6. Candy pile. A giant magnifying lens enlarges one donut, with 3 donuts already in the tray. Job: the hint booster.
7. Yellow-orange animal pile. Meteors rain in, and a flame booster shows a fill meter. Job: the destruction booster.
8. Green fruit pile. A cartoon pointing hand taps an enlarged watermelon, with bananas in the tray. Job: show the control (tap).
9. Purple pile. A magnet with lightning pulls three enlarged rainbow balloons. Job: the magnet booster. The balloon also bookends the balloon in shot 1.

Weaknesses: shot 1 never shows how to play. Five dark, uncaptioned shots in a row feel samey and grim at thumbnail size. The timer and "level 118" read as pressure and grind.
composition_recipe:
CAPTIONED SHOT GRID (shots 2-4, measured at 997px tall):
- 0-5%: breathing room. The background is darkest here so white type has contrast.
- 5.2-7.8%: a single caption line, centered, with 7-8% side margins. The line width floats with word count, from about 57% to 85% of canvas width, while the type size stays fixed.
- 11-18%: the game's own goal UI (1-4 small cards), lifted off the HUD and floated under the caption as a sub-caption or answer key.
- 20-82%: the hero pile. It bleeds left and right, is dense but zoomed in (about 35-45 objects, each 12-25% of canvas width), and the whole mass is roughly rectangular.
- 83-88%: the collection tray, kept as-is from the game.
- 89-95%: the booster bar, kept as-is.
Nothing at the very bottom edge.

Hero pile rules:
- The game's backdrop is replaced by a theme-colored vertical gradient.
- Objects keep soft contact shadows, so the pile reads as a physical heap.
- One focal state per shot (tray filling, boosters unlocking).

HERO SHOT (1):
- Logo in the upper third.
- A diagonal S-road leads the eye from the bottom right up to the hero vehicle at 35-70%.
- Four depth layers: soft pastel landmarks and clouds (back), the hero vehicle and item pile (mid), flying items breaking outward (mid-front), and an oversized foreground bush cropped at the bottom-left corner (front).
- A balloon near the top-right corner balances the logo.

GAMEPLAY SHOTS (5-9):
- The unedited HUD takes 0-15% (level, timer, currency), the goal row 9-15%, the board 17-85% and the tray 87-91%.
- One oversized hero object (or a trio) sits in the central third, plus one effect prop (lens, magnet, hand, meteors) entering from an edge.

Reusable for Comet Garden:
- Caption band at 4-14% (two lines are fine).
- A floating game-UI chip at 15-20%, such as the landing-spot aim tag or a recipe chip.
- The planet as the hero, 80-90% of canvas width, centered at about 52%.
- The real bottom projectile queue kept at 86-94% as an honesty anchor.
- A star-dust background layer for depth.
- On creature close-ups, crop into the planet's surface so each creature is 12-18% of canvas width.
type_recipe:
What they do:
- Heavy, rounded geometric sans, all caps, pure white.
- A soft dark drop shadow, a few px offset down, tinted toward the background hue.
- One line of 4-5 words.
- Cap height about 2.6% of canvas height (about 73px caps on a 2796px canvas, roughly a 100px font).
- Slightly tight tracking, centered, top edge at about 5.2%.
- Exactly one token is recolored: the number. The accent is taken from a hue inside the pile (pink yarn, yellow ducks, blue slippers), so caption and art feel like one image.
- Constant size across the trio. The line width changes with the words, not the type size.
- The voice is a chained run of questions. Two start as counting questions (the "Can you find" style), and the third opens with "And", which carries across the swipe.
- No subtitle, no punctuation other than "?".
- Weakness: the caption is small for search thumbnails, and 6 of 9 shots have none.

Comet Garden recipe:
- Keep one recolored token, but color-code the land or biome word by its in-game color (forest green, sea blue, magma orange, ice cyan). The caption then teaches the recipe.
- Go bigger: cap height about 3.5-4%, up to 2 lines in the 4-14% band.
- Use our own Fredoka Bold in sentence case (softer and cozier) instead of all-caps shouting. White with a soft shadow tinted from the background.
- Replace their counting questions with our own continuation device. Two options:
  1. A cause-to-effect ellipsis chain across shots 1-3: fling, then grow, then who moves in.
  2. A recipe riddle shown as a mini equation (forest chip + sea chip = ?), revealed on the next shot.
- Caption every shot.
color_light_recipe:
Challenge trio:
- Each shot gets one jewel-tone vertical gradient: dark at the top and bottom, lighter in a broad band behind the pile, like a soft spotlight. Sampled values:
  - purple, #4c275d at top to #73409c at mid
  - teal, #014359 to #00728c
  - navy, #00306e to #004d9c
- The key move: the background is roughly the COMPLEMENT of the pile's dominant hue (yellow ducks on deep teal, orange dog gear on navy, white/pink/blue cat props on purple). The objects pop without any outlines.

Objects:
- Glossy soft-plastic or clay 3D look, highly saturated.
- Soft key light from the upper left, gentle ambient occlusion and contact shadows, no hard specular glare.

Hero objects:
- A warm gold-white rim glow plus sparkle particles, and a 2-3x scale-up. Only the story-critical object glows.

Shot 1:
- High-key sky blue (#30b5f6) with a warm yellow and blue logo.
- Background landmarks fade to pastel (aerial perspective), and the foreground is saturated green.

Gameplay quintet:
- A neutral charcoal (#303030) field.
- Each board is curated to ONE color family (red, candy multi, yellow-orange, green, purple), so the set still scrolls as a sequence of color chapters.

For Comet Garden:
- Give each shot its own gradient keyed as the complement of the planet's dominant biome: a green forest world on warm apricot or coral, a blue ocean world on peach, orange magma on deep indigo, icy cyan on rose.
- Our twist: gradients read as a twilight sky (lighter horizon band behind the planet, deeper at the top for the caption). A faint layer of stars and sparkle dust gives depth that their plain fields lack.
- Rim-light the one hero comet or creature per shot in warm gold.
- Never use a flat dark gray field.
character_staging:
- Animals are not mascots. They are matchable objects mixed into the heap (about 6-20 among 40 items), but every cute face is rotated toward the camera and left unblocked, even in a supposedly random pile.
- Expressions are open and happy: big eyes, tongues out, heads tilted.
- Species are clustered with props that tell their story (cats with yarn and milk, ducks with bath toys, dogs with bowls and squeaky toys). Each shot is a mini world.
- Collected animals line up in the tray as a small trophy row (3 ducks).
- The hero shot has no characters at all. The vehicle and its cargo carry the charm.
- The only hand is a cartoon tutorial pointer in shot 8.

For Comet Garden:
- Stage creatures on their matching land (goat on a mountain peak, otters at the forest-sea shoreline, turtles by a volcano-sea edge). Each shot then teaches a habitat recipe.
- Turn all faces to camera, and keep eyes clear of the caption band and the UI chips.
- Scale one hero creature to about 1.5-2x with a rim glow, mid-hop or waving as it moves in. Keep the others at in-game scale for honesty.
- Have creatures peek over the planet's horizon to break the circle's silhouette.
- Use the same hero creature in the first and last shot as a bookend.
what_makes_it_work: The caption chain is a game the shopper plays with their eyes: it asks a question, the next shot continues it with 'And', and the swipe becomes the answer
One recolored token per caption (the number) gives an instant focal point, and its color is taken from the pile, so caption and art bind together
The background is the complement of the pile's dominant hue, so dense heaps of objects still read clearly at thumbnail size without outlines
The piles are zoomed until single objects are 12-25% of canvas width. Cute faces are readable even in search results
The game's own UI (goal cards, tray, booster bar) is kept but rearranged: goal cards float under the caption as an answer key, which reads as honest and instantly signals the genre
Progression is told through UI state across shots: padlocked boosters, then partly unlocked, then all unlocked, with escalating numbers (small, larger, largest)
It freezes the frame one beat before the payoff (3 ducks in the tray, burgers mid-flight to the tray), which feels kinetic in a still image
Each theme is a tiny self-contained world (pets with their stuff), so every shot feels like new content rather than the same level again
Each later shot demonstrates exactly one juicy effect, with one oversized glowing hero object against a sea of small ones
The same motif (a rainbow balloon) appears in the first and last shot, giving the set a sense of design and closure
transferable_to_comet_garden: Continuation captions across shots 1-3, in our own voice. Either a cause-to-effect ellipsis chain (fling a comet... grow a forest by the sea... and who moves in?) or a recipe riddle with a forest chip plus a sea chip equal to '?', where the next shot reveals otters. It uses our actual neighbor-recipe mechanic, not counting
Color-code one keyword per caption with its biome color from the game (forest green, sea blue, magma orange, ice cyan). The caption styling then teaches the land system

A per-shot gradient background in the complement of the planet's dominant biome color, lighter behind the planet and deeper at the top for the white caption. Add faint stars and sparkle dust for our cozy space style

Lift one real UI element out of the HUD and float it under the caption as the answer key: the on-planet aim tag (land plus creature plus points) or a recipe chip. Keep the real bottom projectile queue as an honesty anchor
Zoom so each creature reads at thumbnail size: planet at 80-90% of canvas width, and at least one creature close-up that crops into the planet's surface
Show progression through state instead of words: the same seeded planet goes from bare to sprouting to lush across shots 1-3, and the Lifebook visibly fills in a later shot
Freeze the pre-payoff beat: a comet a hair before impact with the shockwave ring just starting, or a creature mid-hop with its 'moved in' pop
One hero object per shot scaled about 1.5-2x with a warm gold rim glow, everything else at true game scale
Give each later shot a single effect showcase with its own dominant hue: Fusion steam, Combo chain, Meteor finale, Bubble Moon bank shot. Unlike them, caption every one
Explain the gesture once, visually: a soft touch dot with a dotted pull-back trail on the slingshot in shot 1, drawn in our style, not as a cartoon glove
Bookend the set with the same hero creature in shot 1 and in the final no-ads / grown-ups shot

Improve on them: never spend slot 1 on a logo-only scene (fuse the logo or name with the fling mechanic), never show timers, level-100+ numbers or booster inventory counts, and never run several dark uncaptioned shots in a row
do_not_copy: The stacked two-tone chunky wordmark (blue top word over a yellow-orange bottom word) on a dark navy rounded plate
The road-trip hero: an overloaded little car on a winding road with world landmarks (Statue of Liberty, pastel Eiffel Tower, palm) and a rainbow hot-air balloon
Their caption formulas: counting questions of the 'Can you find N' or 'Where are N' kind, followed by an 'And N' continuation with the number recolored
The pets-themed challenge trio (cats, then ducks, then dogs) and its jewel-tone background sequence (purple, then teal, then navy)
Gray rounded-square goal cards with a count in the top-left corner, the 7-slot gray collection tray and the bottom booster bar (magnet, screw, fan, frozen clock) with padlock or count badges
The flat charcoal gameplay field with a teal LEVEL label, clock-icon countdown and crown counter
Their booster visuals: a magnifying lens over the pile, a red-and-blue magnet throwing lightning, meteors raining with a fill meter
The white cartoon pointing hand used as a tutorial cursor
Gold rim-glow trios with sparkle trails flying into a tray (use our own impact and shockwave language instead)
Heaps of glossy 3D household objects as the visual identity (keep our 2D vector planet, biomes and critters)
